notes:
What's new in Vekrun 0.7.9

This release also brings everything prepared for 0.7.8, which was not published on its own.

Faster from Start
• A small fix in a project Vekrun has seen before took about 36–44 seconds from Start to verified proof in development measurements with Codex, down from 88–107 seconds in 0.7.7. Four tasks, every result checked by an independent evaluator in a fresh VM.
• The main cause was a warm-up step that failed silently, so every Node project started cold. It now works, and warm bases outlive their run.
• A pre-booted spare VM, machine-wide VM and memory limits (so several Vekrun windows don't starve each other), and overlapping work for single-agent runs.
• The Coordinator now uses the model you assigned to it (Settings, Factory models). Before, scope advice and other Coordinator turns always ran the agent's default model.
• A warm project's build no longer waits for the baseline test run to show that the suite starts, once that test command has started in a build machine from the same setup. The baseline still runs beside the build, and a suite that can't start is still reported when the change is tested.
• Choosing between one agent and a Council reuses the agent check routing made moments earlier.
• Every run says which speed mechanisms it used and, if one wasn't used, why. `vekrun factory timings` shows each wait, measured from Start, including a "Baseline start check" line.
• Not reached: a medium task (our M1) took 70–92 seconds, short of the 2× raw-agent target we set. Speed with Claude Code has not been measured yet.
• No check was removed or weakened for speed.

Context Compiler (experiments, off by default)
• Each agent role can be handed a compiled context packet: the code, tests, decisions and Memory that matter for its job, with where each came from and what was left out and why. A packet is reused only when nothing it was built from has changed.
• A structured Council state, a shared evidence workspace for reads at a revision, and leaner agent instructions are available as separate experiments.
• Memory learnings carry their proof. A learning that no longer holds is shown as such, never as current, and an agent's unchecked claim is labelled as a claim.
• Context prepared, in the Work Item inspector, shows what each role received and why. The budget card adds the actual usage the providers reported per role, including cached input; unknowns are shown as unknown, never zero.
• Try them in Improvement Lab. They stay off until paired measurements show they save tokens without lowering the quality of the work.

Budgets you can see
• One ledger for every model call — Coordinator, Council, builders, checks, reviews — with budgets by owner. Calls that used to go unmetered now count.
• A budget card on each Work Item shows what each role spent, the model it ran and why. Only you, in the main window, can add budget.
• A preferred model for each signed-in coding agent.

Safer setup and delivery
• Supply-chain checks can no longer be switched off to get setup through — not directly, and not indirectly through environment variables, settings files, wrapper scripts or encoded commands. Vekrun turns any weakened setting back on and fails the step. A project file that turns one off (for example `strict-ssl=false` in `.npmrc`) fails the proof with a plain reason.
• An agent's administrator change to the VM waits for your approval.
• Existing projects are set up the way their own files declare. The agent starts only once the project's tests can start.
• A desktop or mobile app whose native checks on this Mac were blocked can no longer be accepted or delivered because its Linux checks passed, and is never shown as "Outcome verified".
• Credentials are removed from what agents are handed from Memory and the code map, leaving the surrounding code as it is.

Sign-in
• Vekrun now recognises a project's sign-in (Devise, Auth.js, allauth or Breeze) and keeps it, or adds the framework's default when the work asks for sign-in and none is there. Mailpit and test-only secrets come with it.
• Sign-in is checked in a fresh VM: sign up, sign in and out, a protected page redirect, password reset by email, a session that survives a restart, and wrong-password and CSRF checks. The results are Proof Pack rows.
• A brand-new project no longer stops at the readiness check before its agent has created the app.
• New: `vekrun factory slice --verify-only` verifies an existing implementation without an agent turn.

Terminal
• The terminal has a visible place to type again: it takes focus when shown, keeps an outline cursor when not, and offers "Click to type".
• A new session opens with a small VEKRUN TERMINAL banner saying where commands run, with the prompt at the bottom.
• New: "Open terminal in this VM" (Work Item menu) and "Open terminal at this step" (Proof). It starts read-only; only you, in the app, can allow changes. Files changed by hand reach a proof only through Keep and re-verify, or are discarded.

Workflows
• The Workflows page is simpler: a gallery led by the runs in progress, then one workflow at a time. Pick a workflow, answer its one question and press Run workflow.
• What happens lists each step once in plain words, with parallel steps, conditions and approvals visible.
• One "+ New workflow" button and one ⋯ menu per workflow; the per-workflow section is now called Automations.

Light theme, Live Share and Preview
• A full light theme with a switch in the top bar. One primary button style everywhere; disabled buttons look disabled.
• Desktop apps can be shared on Live Share, as simulators are. Desktop Preview has plain failure messages, a desktop frame, and a project you trust once no longer asks again.
• The app stays responsive while a large project is indexed: status checks that ran on the main thread no longer do, and polls never pile up.

Smaller fixes
• GitHub's card shows its CLI state only, never also "Not connected".
• Deployment shows each provider's own full-colour logo.
• Git ref names stay readable in redacted lines; real secrets are still redacted.
